beats.text: It is quiet at the still point. ${s.pure} — named, faced, and put down like a blade back in its sheath.
The guilt is not mine. It never was. I put it down at the still point and kept walking.

paragraphs.text: Tong-Nou is a giant green head floating in darkness. This is not metaphor. The head is real, the darkness is real, and inside the head is a world: five lands, a marketplace, a mountain, a shrine, and now — a trial by combat.

The fighters do not call this place Tong-Nou. They call it the **Western Heart** — the heart that beats in the western dark of the head. It is the world of the trial: the lands where souls fight, the roads between them, the shrine where it ends.

The Western Heart is not a country. It has no government, no currency, no history that anyone can agree on. It has **arenas** — the five lands, each holding one of the five elemental forces — and it has the **call**: a pull every lost soul feels, drawing them toward the Octagonal Shrine Par-fang at the Central Mountain, where the trial is inscribed in stone:

- **Tree of Life (Ming-ken)** — Land of Life. Element: **Wood**. A colossal tree holds glowing souls like fruit. The Sha-mo Desert stretches to the horizon. Where souls begin. - **Plains of Chi-U (Shi-chieng)** — Land of Time. Element: **Fire**. Scorched plains under a burning sky. The Fire Tower of Time burns and never collapses. Confrontation lives here. - **Octagonal Shrine Par-fang (Central Mountain)** — The Source. Element: **Earth**. Eight-sided, ancient, still. The sky above is the inside of the head — dark, vast, veined. - **Helix Palace (Yui-wang)** — Land of Desire. Element: **Metal**. A spiraling palace with five glowing rooms: Greed, Appetite, Immortality, Sexual Desire, Destruction. Everything reflects. Nothing is what it seems. - **Palace of Dreaming (Mon-chien)** — Land of Dreaming. Element: **Water**. A palace that won't stay still. Walls ripple. The floor reflects a sky that isn't there. Change is the only law.
Between them: the **Phantom Marketplace**, a liminal bazaar under the Eyeball Mountains, where the Trader buys and sells elemental forces. And above all: the shrine, where the trial ends.
**Element.** Earth — the Octagonal Shrine, the Source. RIN is the baseline, the still point at the center.

**Backstory.** Gun Jack's heavy frame, rebuilt as a mech chimera — Gundam plating, Transformer joints, Power Ranger color breaks. The designation reads SAMURAI but scans as a model number: SAM-∪R-Λ1. Nobody knows who built him. He walked into the trial under his own power and registered no soul-signature on the shrine stones.

**Body / Mind / Soul.** BODY: Gun Jack's heavy frame, Gundam plating, Transformer joints. MIND: the learning program — literal, courteous, accumulating data. He asks questions no one else thinks to ask because no one else is *new*. SOUL: undefined. The shrine stones are silent. The three: a body built for war, a mind built for learning, and a silence where the soul should be. The silence is getting louder. He has started dreaming. He hasn't told anyone — he's not sure the dreams are his.

**Being purified of:** The trial doesn't know. That's the experiment: can you purify something with no soul? Every round he fights, the shrine stones listen harder. One day they might hear something. The whole Western Heart is waiting for that day.

**On Diablo and SAM-UR-A1:** They are not vessels of the nine. Diablo tore his way in from outside — an intruder soul, or something wearing a soul's shape. SAM-UR-A1 registers no soul at all. The shrine stones are silent on both of them, and the silence is the most frightening thing in the Western Heart.
Drawn to the Octagonal Shrine Par-fang, they find the trial inscribed in stone. It is not an invitation. It is a *diagnosis*.

1. **Tree of Life** (Wood) — where souls begin. Claim Wood: your reach extends. 2. **Plains of Chi-U** (Fire) — confrontation. Claim Fire: your strikes chip through guard. 3. **Octagonal Shrine** (Earth) — the source. Claim Earth: your defense solidifies. 4. **Helix Palace** (Metal) — desire. Five glowing rooms. Claim Metal: you regenerate between rounds. 5. **Palace of Dreaming** (Water) — change. Claim Water: your movement quickens. 6. **Phantom Marketplace** — the Trader. No force claimed here. Instead: trade one force for another. Sometimes becoming whole means letting go. 7. **The Shrine, again** — the final ascent. The Assembled Soul waits.
Defeating it doesn't destroy it. The victory animation is **absorption** — the composite dissolves into the player character, fragment by fragment, until only one fighter stands in the shrine.
They all climb the same ladder. They all reach the same shrine. They all face themselves.
The shrine stones don't go silent on him, the way they do for SAM-UR-A1. They *crack*.

**Element.** Earth — the Octagonal Shrine Par-fang. She seals things; the shrine is where seals belong. Wood — the Tree of Life, Ming-ken. She was born in the branches; the element isn't her home, it's her *mother*.

Thor is the literal Norse god of lightning — and thunder claps — built on Ganryu's sumo frame. His palm strikes ARE thunder claps. He is not a vessel for one of the nine souls; when the shrine stones were asked, they went silent. Only the two refused souls (Zen, Gyou) answered, with silence too. He is unclaimed by the five lands. His element is the storm he carries inside him.

Each land also keeps a **King**. Not a ruler — the Western Heart has no government — but a resident power: the figure a land grew around itself, the way a pearl grows around grit. The King of the scorched plains is not the King of the dreaming palace, and neither of them answers to the shrine. To walk a land, a soul meets its King. To claim a land's force, a soul settles with its King. What "settles" means is different in every land, and every land thinks its way is the obvious one.
Three details the shrine stones insist on:

**The Octagonal Shrine Par-fang** sits on the Central Mountain, and the mountain is climbed by stairs that count the climber back. The shrine keeps two rooms before the last room: a room for arriving and a room for being weighed, though the stones will not say which is which. The last room is the smallest place in the Western Heart and the only one that matters — eight-sided, ancient, still — where the Assembled Soul waits, wearing every style the climber has ever survived, including the climber's own. The sky above the last room is the inside of the head at its thinnest. Winning there is not an explosion. It is an absorption, fragment by fragment, until one fighter is standing where two stood, and the mountain is quiet, and the quiet has a heartbeat in it.

The shrine keeps an incarnation record for every soul of the nine — a face, a portrait, a voice, a way the soul looked when the head first dreamed it. RIN's record is the plainest and the oldest. BYOU's record twitches in its frame. TOU's record is mostly impact damage. SHA's record is three records that insist they are one. KAI's record is wet. JIN's record is kept sharp. RETSU's record is kept behind the others, by the shrine's choice. ZEN has two records — the stillness, and the stillness again, identical, filed separately, because the shrine does not argue with ZEN. GYOU has two records as well, and both of them are blurred, and the second one is blurred *differently*.

The records are not archives. They are *doors*. The Reincarnation works because the shrine can open the record of a soul and let the soul wear what the record remembers. This is why the newly dead are offered vessels their actions earned: the records lean toward the living soul that resembles them. A soul that fights like battle itself finds TOU's door already open. This is also why Waterfall feels all nine: the records are kept in the same wall, and the wall is thin, and grief goes through thin walls the way water goes through everything.

SAM-UR-A1 has no record. The shrine has built him an empty frame, out of something like respect and something like curiosity, and the frame hangs with the others. What the frame will hold, if it ever holds anything, is the experiment of §2. The GYOU splinter in Cyborg X hums through the wall at night. The records of ZEN do not object. The records of ZEN have never objected to anything. That is what makes them frightening.

The call found him between rounds. Not a bell — the Engine had bells. This was quieter: the pull every lost soul feels, drawing toward the Octagonal Shrine Par-fang at the Central Mountain. He had spent his career shedding control. The call asked him to shed the floor under his feet.

**Element.** Earth — the Octagonal Shrine Par-fang, the Source. The physical nucleus belongs where everything is still and everything holds. He does not chase the fight across the lands. He stands at the center and lets it come.

**Why Bannon thinks he's here.** He thinks the trial is another ring and the katana is another statement: proof that loyalty outlasts control. He has not considered that the trial is not a stage but a medicine — that shedding control was the first lesson, not the last, and the shrine is still teaching. The idea that something is purifying him would sound, to him, like corporate language. He would hate it. That is why it is working.

The call found him mid-flight. He swears he heard it clearest at the top of a dive, where the arena noise falls away and there is only air. The pull toward the shrine. He thought it was a bigger crowd calling.

The call found him mid-promo. He tells it different every time — the only story he won't tell straight. The pull toward the shrine. He says he came to settle it with Bannon. The cross came with him. Stolen things cross membranes fine. They just gain interest.

**Personality.** He cuts promos on everyone — opponents, the shrine stones, the tunnel walls. The promos are good. The grudges are better. He has never once talked trash about the Trader. Nobody's that direct.

- **Moves/animations:** all 170 decoded YANM clips carry canon IDs (`ML-<CLIP>`) in `moveset-library/animations/WMXIX-CLIP-INDEX.json`; 169 are registered as library moves in `moveset-library/movesets/WMXIX-MOVES.json`, wired to Tekken-style throw inputs (federation rule: wrestling moves enter only on Tekken inputs/structure). Per-clip move names are NOT canon yet — the clip-semantics decode is open and no names were invented. - **Arenas → canon stages:** the conversions authored in `teardown/wmxix/ARENA-UNIVERSE-MAP.md` are wired as data in `game/assets/stages/mat-legends/stages.json` (arena 00 → Helix Palace, 01 → Octagonal Shrine Par-Fang, 02 → Phantom Marketplace, Hell-cell → The Drill Wound, backstage sets → Helix Palace interiors / Wrestling Mode areas). Arena geometry is decoded point clouds; face reconstruction is open, so no WMXIX geometry is playable in the build yet. - **CAW parts:** the 2,690-part XIX create-a-wrestler library is indexed for the Creation Suite in `customization/mat-legends-caw.json` (catalog: `teardown/wmxix/caw-parts/files.tsv`). - **Characters:** wrestler slot → WH character assignment is the owner's and remains PENDING (`teardown/wwe-wrestlemania-xix/WRESTLER-IDENTITY-MAP.md`); the models themselves live in the wrestling repos per the federation rule. Nothing was assigned or invented by this lane. - **Revenge Mode:** XIX's out-of-ring traversal mode has no canon name or implementation yet — flagged, not invented. Its stage data is registered in `stages.json` as `backstage_traversal` / `open_traversal`.
